message: The plan passed grounding validation (this does not prove that any proposal is correct or safe).

proposals.title: Review Query Construction for Potential SQL Injection
proposals.description: Examine application source code handling search endpoints to ensure parameterization or proper neutralization of special elements is used, as referenced in CWE-89.
proposals.problem_addressed: Potential SQL injection handling of user-controllable input in search paths.

affected_area.description: Endpoints /search and /api/search observed in application and nginx logs.

proposals.rationale: The finding is hypothesis_not_confirmed. Suspicious request text is observed activity, not confirmed exploitation. Reference material from CWE-89 and CAPEC-66 indicates that applications utilizing user-controllable input without proper neutralization in SQL commands can be vulnerable to SQL injection.
proposals.reference_support_limits: The reference passages describe CWE-89 and CAPEC-66 generally and do not establish that the specific code in this incident is vulnerable or that exploitation succeeded. The finding is hypothesis_not_confirmed.

severity.rationale: Severity is judged as medium based on typical consequences of CWE-89, though no exploitation is confirmed in this incident.

proposals.expected_security_effect: Reviewing and hardening query construction helps reduce the risk of improper neutralization of special elements used in SQL commands.
operational_side_effects: Code modifications may require thorough testing of search functionality before deployment.

implementation_steps.text: Review application source code for database query construction practices.
Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for handling user-controllable input as described in CWE-89.

preconditions: Human review and authorization required before modifying source code.
unresolved_questions: Does the application source code properly parameterize database queries for /search and /api/search?

validation.procedure: Perform code review and run parameterized query unit tests in an authorized staging environment.
validation.expected_result: Queries successfully handle input safely without executing unintended SQL commands.

confidence.rationale: The finding is unconfirmed: suspicious requests are observed activity, not confirmed exploitation.

priority_basis.ordering_rule: Proposals are ordered by, in turn: (1) evidence linkage, incident_linked before general_hardening; (2) severity, high before medium before low before unknown; (3) disruption, low before medium before high before unknown; (4) reversibility, reversible before partially_reversible before unknown before irreversible; (5) the order in which the model returned them.

unresolved_questions: Were the requests observed in application-4 and nginx-19 processed by vulnerable database query logic?
limitations: Analysis is based on observed request patterns and hypotheses; no database query logs or source code were inspected.
priority_criteria: priority_rank is an ORDINAL position under a fixed, documented rule; it is not a risk score, a probability or a measured exposure.

Proposals are ordered by, in turn: (1) evidence linkage, incident_linked before general_hardening; (2) severity, high before medium before low before unknown; (3) disruption, low before medium before high before unknown; (4) reversibility, reversible before partially_reversible before unknown before irreversible; (5) the order in which the model returned them.

The severity, disruption and reversibility ratings are the model's own, uncalibrated judgements. The evidence linkage is computed from the citations: a proposal is incident_linked only if it cites at least one observed evidence id.
plan.confidence_meaning: Confidence is the model's own ordinal judgement (low, medium, high) of how well the cited incident evidence, hypotheses, configuration facts and reference passages support THIS proposal. It is not a probability, it is not calibrated against any measurement, and it says nothing about whether the proposal would work. 'high' is refused by validation unless a linked hypothesis is confirmed and configuration facts are available; 'medium' needs at least one step stated by a cited reference.
caveats: This plan is advisory. Every proposal is a proposal only: nothing was executed, no file or container was changed and no test was launched.
Hypotheses stay hypotheses. A proposal does not confirm a root cause, and reference passages are general knowledge that neither confirm nor refute what happened in the incident.
Reference passages come from a small curated CWE/CAPEC subset and cannot be treated as comprehensive Docker, Juice Shop or configuration-hardening guidance.
Grounding validation checks that identifiers exist and sit in the right category and screens some high-risk wording; it does not prove that a recommendation is correct, sufficient or safe.
Whether a proposal reduces risk has not been tested; validation belongs to a later phase and its success under tested conditions would not be a universal security guarantee.

validation.note: Validation checks that identifiers exist and sit in the right category, that proposals are honest about missing configuration and risk, and screens some high-risk wording. It does not prove that a recommendation is correct, sufficient or safe.
